claims.statement: Legendre first published least-squares method in 1805 appendix pp72-74
1806 supplemented Legendre text must not be conflated with 1805 first edition
Legendre identified overdetermined inconsistent observation equations and minimization of sums of squared residuals
Gauss 1809 Theoria motus gave a probability-error interpretation of least squares
Gauss claimed prior private use circa 1795, a priority issue requiring separation from first publication
Gauss 1801 Ceres orbit reconstruction involved more than one least-squares calculation
Robert Adrain independently treated error probabilities in 1808
Modern Q(a)=Σ(y-a)² is minimized by arithmetic mean; example 9,10,14 gives a=11 Q=14
Modern absolute deviations are minimized by median; example 9,10,14 median10 gives absolute error5
Linear fit of x=0,1,2 and y=1,2,2 has a=7/6, b=1/2 and residual squared sum1/6
Independent homoscedastic Gaussian-error maximum likelihood is equivalent to least squares
Unequal variances motivate weighted least squares; correlations or model misspecification can invalidate simple claims
Modern normal-equation and residual-orthogonality symbols are later conceptual apparatus
